- White mold-like material visible at the tip of the ear

Key candidates: **Ear_rots_Diplodia** (bleached husks, white mold on ear) or **Diplodia_stalk_rot** (premature plant death + stalk rot). Let me compare reference images.
Ear_rots_Diplodia reference shows bleached husks and white mold on kernels — very similar to the test image. Let me also check one more candidate given the widespread plant death.

Goss's wilt shows streaked/yellowed leaves and bacterial ooze — doesn't match the test image's fully dead/brown foliage.

**Analysis:**
- Test image: corn ear with bleached white/gray husks pulled back, pale cream kernels, white mold at tip, and completely dead/brown dried foliage throughout plant

- Diplodia_stalk_rot: only shows stalk/lodging damage, not ear rot
- Goss_wilt: shows striped/streaked leaves, not complete plant death with bleached ear
